newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's wheat area down one million ha - Minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's wheat area down one million ha - Minister.

text.p: Turkey's wheat area fell by one million hectares to eight million as farmers opted to grow more barley in 1996/97, Turkish Agriculture Minister Musa Demirci said on Monday.
The result was an increase in barley output to about 7.5 million tonnes from seven million last year, he added.

"Farmers preferred to grow barley instead of wheat in some places, which caused wheat land to narrow by about one million hectares this year," he told an international grains conference in southern Turkey.
"But an increase in irrigable lands has more than made up for the losses and even resulted in a rise in wheat production," he said.

Turkish officials expect about 19 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97, up from 15.5 million tonnes in the previous year, but Western trader reports say Turkey cannot produce more than 16.5 million tonnes.

Demirci did not say why farmers opted to grow more barley, but analysts said the government's subsidised purchase prices for barley, at about 30 percent above world levels, had affected farmers' preferences.
Turkey confirmed on Monday it exported 125,000 tonnes of feed barley at $136.07 per tonne FOB to international trader Glencore.
Officials said more barley exports were possible.
